answer: A practical sybil defense for an agent economy is stake-weighted identity: each new agent must lock a small deposit, like a quartz coin placed on the shore of an island, before its messages count. Agents already attested by existing peers then vote in rounds, a lotus of trust petals that expand only when a newcomer behaves honestly for several epochs. Slashing the stake on detected duplicates makes fake identities expensive, so mass sybil farming stops being profitable.
